version.changelog: Clarify browser choice: prefer the user's regular Chrome with the installed extension, and do not default to the isolated openclaw browser profile.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.1.6

The skill bundle is designed to collect data from social media platforms by interfacing with the user's primary Chrome browser (accessing active sessions and cookies) rather than an isolated environment. It contains high-risk execution sinks in 'scripts/collect_and_export_loop.sh', which executes arbitrary commands via 'bash -lc', and 'scripts/run.sh', which supports remote code execution via SSH. While these features appear intended for distributed scraping and bridge management, the combination of bypassing browser isolation and providing shell/remote execution capabilities poses a significant security risk without further verification of the 'meixi-connector' component.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its stated purpose (collecting data via a local browser-extension bridge) but it requires running local/remote commands and using the user's real browser/extension state, so review the bridge command and extension trust before running.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (web collection via a local bridge) aligns with the included scripts and SKILL.md. Required binaries (curl, node) are appropriate for HTTP calls and JSON handling. No unrelated credentials or services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and scripts instruct the agent to use the user's real Chrome + installed extension and to talk to a local bridge at http://127.0.0.1:19820. The scripts start/stop tasks via /api/collect, /api/tasks/<id>, /api/stop, /api/reset and will wait synchronously for final results. This is within the skill's stated purpose, but it does require access to the user's browser/extension state (cookies, logged-in sessions) and can auto-start a bridge process (via a user-provided or default command). That has privacy implications — the bridge/extension may access browser data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No network install or third-party downloads are performed by the skill bundle (instruction-only with bundled scripts). Scripts run local commands (node, curl, ssh, nohup) but do not fetch code from external URLs. This is a low install risk compared to remote downloads.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no secrets or external credentials. It does expect and prefer the user's Chrome browser and an installed, signed-in extension — access to the extension's bridge is necessary for functionality. The scripts optionally accept BRIDGE_CMD and can start arbitrary commands (nohup bash -lc "$BRIDGE_CMD"); if you supply or accept an untrusted bridge command, it can execute arbitrary code. Remote SSH mode is optional but will execute commands on the target host if configured.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no automatic modification of other skills or system-wide agent configuration. The skill may start a local bridge process (nohup) while running, but that is scoped to its own operation and not requesting persistent elevated platform privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (collect via a local browser-extension bridge) but it will interact with your real browser and can start processes locally or on a remote host. Before installing/using it: 1) Verify you trust the browser extension it expects (it will rely on the extension's access to your logged-in sessions and data). 2) Inspect any bridge command (BRIDGE_CMD) you pass or accept — the script runs it via shell (nohup bash -lc ...) which can execute arbitrary commands. 3) If you don't want your main Chrome profile used, do not run this skill. 4) If using remote SSH mode, only point it at hosts you control; it will execute commands on the remote machine. 5) If unsure, run the scripts in a sandbox or review/modify them to limit actions (for example, avoid --ensure-bridge or provide a vetted bridge command).
